{{Quote|Your handmaidens are trained to protect you. Let me show you.''"<br />"''I want to be trained too.|Captain Panaka and Queen Padmé Amidala, as the latter viewed her handmaidens' battle dresses|<ref name="Queen in Disguise" />}}
'''Battle dresses''' were [[Clothing/Legends|clothing]] worn [[Monarch of Naboo/Legends|Monarch of Naboo]] and [[Gender/Legends|her]] [[Handmaiden/Legends|handmaidens]] to engage in combat.<ref name="TPM junior">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (junior novelization)|''Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace'' junior novelization]]</ref> During [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala's]] reign as the [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], they were worn as training uniforms by her handmaidens. When [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Quarsh Panaka/Legends|Quarsh Panaka]], the leader of Amidala's [[Royal Naboo Security Forces/Legends|security forces]], suggested that she observe her handmaidens during their combat training, Amidala decided to participate by disguising herself in the same [[Color|maroon]] and gold training uniform.<ref name="Queen in Disguise" />

During the [[Invasion of Naboo|invasion]] by the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]], the handmaidens' battle dresses were worn by Amidala and four of her handmaidens while the Queen's decoy, [[Sabé/Legends|Sabé]], wore the royal red and black battle dress.<ref name="Episode I" />

Amidala wore a maroon battle dress for another [[Skirmish on Naboo/Legends|skirmish]] on her homeworld when she was the [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] of Naboo during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="Shadow Warrior">{{TCW|Shadow Warrior}}</ref>

{{Clothes-stub}}

==Behind the scenes==
Battle dresses were created for the [[1999]] [[prequel trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']].<ref name="Episode I" /> The costumes were first identified as battle dress in the [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (junior novelization)|junior novelization]], written by [[Patricia C. Wrede]] and released [[May 3]] of the same year.<ref name="TPM junior" /> The designs were conceptualized by artist [[Iain McCaig]] and the finished costumes were realized by costume designer [[Trisha Biggar]] and her department. McCaig's initial concept featured straps across the belly, but they were removed from subsequent concepts as they would be awkward and uncomfortable to wear in reality.<ref name="The Art of Episode I">''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace]]''</ref>

[[Hasbro]] created an action figure<ref name="Sabe (Queen's Decoy)">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: Power of the Jedi|pack=Sabé (Queen's Decoy)|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/potjsabe.asp}}</ref> and a doll of Sabé in her battle dress, though the latter's packaging purported to be one of Queen Amidala herself.<ref name="Ultimate Hair Queen Amidala">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: Episode I (toy line)|text=''Star Wars: Episode I'' (Queen Amidala Collection)|pack=Ultimate Hair Queen Amidala|altlink=https://www.amazon.com/Star-Wars-Episode-Ultimate-Amidala/dp/B00000J2DI}}</ref> They also created multiple action figures of Padmé in hers.<ref name="Queen Amidala (Naboo)">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: Episode I (toy line)|pack=Queen Amidala (Naboo)|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/episodeIamidalanaboo.asp}}</ref><ref name="Queen Amidala (Battle)">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: Episode I (toy line)|pack=Queen Amidala (Battle)|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/episodeIamidalabattle.asp}}</ref><ref name="Defense of Naboo">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: Episode I (toy line)|text=''Star Wars: Episode I'' (Portrait Edition)|pack=Defense of Naboo (Queen Amidala and Qui-Gon Jinn)|altlink=https://waysoftheforce.com/action-figure/2000-queen-amidala-and-qui-gon-jinn-defense-of-naboo}}</ref>
